source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο δεῖ περισσοτέρως προσέχειν ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἀκουσθεῖσιν, μήποτε παραρυῶμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this it is necessary more abundantly to pay attention us to the things heard, lest we drift away.

en.L: Because of this it is necessary [for] us to pay attention more abundantly to the things heard, lest we drift away.
en.B: This is why we must give even greater attention to the things we have heard, so that we do not drift off.
en.R: So we must listen even more carefully to the message we have heard. Then we will not slowly drift away from it.

es.L: Por esto es necesario que nosotros prestemos atención más abundantemente a las cosas oídas, no sea que vayamos a la deriva.
es.B: Por eso debemos prestar una atención todavía mayor a lo que hemos oído, para no irnos a la deriva.
es.R: Así que debemos escuchar con todavía más cuidado el mensaje que hemos oído. Así no nos iremos alejando de él poco a poco.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii inatupasa sisi kuyazingatia kwa wingi zaidi mambo yaliyosikiwa, tusije tukaelea mbali.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo sababu tunapaswa kuyazingatia hata zaidi mambo tuliyoyasikia, ili tusije tukaelea mbali.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tunapaswa kusikiliza kwa makini zaidi ujumbe tuliousikia. Ndipo hatutaelea mbali nao polepole.

decisions.choice: because of this: because the Son is so far above the angels
decisions.reason: "Because of this" draws the lesson from chapter 1. The message God has spoken in the Son (1:2) carries more weight than the message given through angels (2:2), so it calls for closer attention.

decisions.choice: drift away: slip away gradually, like a boat carried past its mooring
decisions.reason: παραρρέω means "flow past, slip away", and was used of a boat drifting off course or of something slipping from the mind. The danger is not open rebellion but slow carelessness, which verse 3 calls "neglect". προσέχω, "pay attention to, hold to", could also be used of bringing a ship in to anchor.

decisions.choice: the things heard: the message of salvation the readers received
decisions.reason: The things heard are the message first spoken by the Lord and passed on to the readers by those who heard him (verse 3).

decisions.choice: slowly drift away from it
decisions.reason: Readable adds "slowly" and "from it" to bring out the picture of gradual drifting (m2).

decisions.choice: ir a la deriva
decisions.reason: "Ir a la deriva" is said of a boat carried along by the current with nothing holding it, the picture of m2, and is also used of people who lose their way little by little.

decisions.choice: tukaelea mbali (drift away)
decisions.reason: "Kuelea mbali" is what a boat does when the current carries it away, which keeps the picture of meaning decision m2. "Kukosa" (miss) or "kupotea" (get lost) would lose the slow, unnoticed movement.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ὁ δι’ ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος, καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν, πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας, ἥτις, ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη, συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν;

records.literal_gloss: If for the through angels having been spoken word was firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense, \v 3 how we will escape so great having neglected a salvation, which, a beginning having received to be spoken through the Lord, by those having heard to us was confirmed, \v 4 bearing witness with [them] the God by signs both and wonders and various powers and of [the] Spirit Holy distributions according to the of him will?

en.L: For if the word spoken through angels was firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense, \v 3 how will we escape, having neglected so great a salvation, which, having received a beginning [in] being spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard, \v 4 God bearing witness with [them] by both signs and wonders and various powers and distributions of [the] Holy Spirit according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will?
en.B: For if the word that was spoken through angels held good, and every breach of it and every refusal to listen met with the penalty it deserved, \v 3 how will we escape if we pay no attention to a salvation as great as this? The Lord was the first to speak of it, and it was made certain to us by those who had listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 4 while God added {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own testimony by signs and wonders, by many kinds of mighty works, and by sharing out the Holy Spirit as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.
en.R: God gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} law through angels, and that message stood firm. Everyone who broke it or refused to obey it was punished as they deserved. \v 3 So how will we escape if we ignore such a great salvation? The Lord Jesus was the first to tell about this salvation. Then the people who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} told it to us and showed us that it is true. \v 4 God also showed that it is true. He did signs and wonders and all kinds of miracles. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave gifts of the Holy Spirit to people, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted.

es.L: Porque si la palabra dicha por medio de ángeles fue firme, y toda transgresión y desobediencia recibió una justa retribución, \v 3 ¿cómo escaparemos nosotros, habiendo descuidado una salvación tan grande, la cual, habiendo recibido [su] comienzo al ser anunciada por medio del Señor, nos fue confirmada por los que oyeron, \v 4 dando Dios testimonio juntamente [con ellos] con señales y prodigios y diversas obras de poder y repartos del Espíritu Santo según {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad?
es.B: Porque si la palabra dicha por medio de ángeles se mantuvo firme, y toda infracción de ella y toda negativa a escuchar recibió el castigo merecido, \v 3 ¿cómo escaparemos nosotros si no hacemos caso de una salvación tan grande? El Señor fue el primero en anunciarla, y nos la confirmaron los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían escuchado, \v 4 mientras Dios añadía {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio testimonio con señales y prodigios, con muchas clases de obras poderosas y repartiendo el Espíritu Santo como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiso.
es.R: Dios dio {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ley por medio de ángeles, y ese mensaje se mantuvo firme. Todo el que la quebrantó o se negó a obedecerla recibió el castigo que merecía. \v 3 Entonces, ¿cómo vamos a escapar nosotros si no hacemos caso de una salvación tan grande? El Señor Jesús fue el primero que habló de esta salvación. Luego los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oyeron nos la anunciaron y nos mostraron que es verdad. \v 4 Dios también mostró que es verdad. Hizo señales y prodigios y toda clase de milagros. Y dio dones del Espíritu Santo a las personas, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiso.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa neno lililonenwa kupitia malaika lilikuwa imara, na kila uvunjaji na ukaidi ulipokea malipo yaliyostahili, \v 3 sisi tutaepukaje, tukiwa tumeupuuza wokovu mkubwa kiasi hiki, ambao, ukiwa umeanza kunenwa kupitia Bwana, ulithibitishwa kwetu na wale waliosikia, \v 4 Mungu akishuhudia pamoja [nao] kwa ishara na maajabu na matendo mbalimbali ya nguvu na kwa migawo ya Roho Mtakatifu kulingana na mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa neno lililonenwa kupitia malaika lilisimama imara, na kila kulivunja na kila kukataa kulisikiliza kulipata adhabu iliyostahili, \v 3 tutaepukaje sisi tukiupuuza wokovu mkubwa kama huu? Bwana ndiye aliyekuwa wa kwanza kuunena, nao ukathibitishwa kwetu na wale waliomsikiliza, \v 4 huku Mungu naye akiongeza ushuhuda {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa ishara na maajabu, kwa matendo ya nguvu ya kila aina, na kwa kugawa Roho Mtakatifu kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyopenda.
sw.R: Mungu alitoa sheria {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kupitia malaika, na ujumbe huo ulisimama imara. Kila aliyeivunja au kukataa kuitii aliadhibiwa kama alivyostahili. \v 3 Basi tutaepukaje tukiupuuza wokovu mkubwa namna hii? Bwana Yesu ndiye aliyekuwa wa kwanza kuwaeleza watu habari za wokovu huu. Kisha wale waliomsikia walituambia habari hizo, wakatuonyesha kwamba ni kweli. \v 4 Mungu naye alionyesha kwamba ni kweli. Alifanya ishara na maajabu na miujiza ya kila aina. Tena aliwapa watu vipawa vya Roho Mtakatifu, kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyotaka.

decisions.choice: the word spoken through angels: the law given at Sinai
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition held that angels were present at the giving of the law (Deuteronomy 33:2 in the Greek; compare Acts 7:38, 53; Galatians 3:19). The author argues from this: if the law brought by angels was binding, the message brought by the Son is more so.

decisions.choice: firm: valid and binding, in force
decisions.reason: βέβαιος was a legal word for what is valid and guaranteed. The verb from the same family appears in verse 3 ("confirmed"): the new message too was made sure.

decisions.choice: transgression and disobedience: stepping over the line, and refusing to listen
decisions.reason: παράβασις is crossing a boundary, breaking a command. παρακοή is literally "hearing amiss", a refusal to listen and obey, which links to the call to pay attention in verse 1.

decisions.choice: argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: "If ... how?" argues from the lesser to the greater: if breaking the law brought sure punishment, neglecting a greater salvation will not go unpunished. Hebrews uses the same pattern in 10:28-29 and 12:25.

decisions.choice: neglected: treated carelessly, paid no attention to
decisions.reason: ἀμελέω means "be unconcerned about, disregard". It is the opposite of the close attention of verse 1, not an open rejection.

decisions.choice: first spoken by the Lord Jesus, then confirmed by those who heard him
decisions.reason: "The Lord" is Jesus, who first announced this salvation in his ministry. The message reached the author and the readers through others who had heard him: the author counts himself with them ("to us") as one who did not hear Jesus in person.

decisions.choice: signs, wonders, and various powers: miracles that confirmed the message
decisions.reason: The three words appear together for the miracles that marked out Jesus and the apostles (Acts 2:22; 2 Corinthians 12:12). "Signs" point to a meaning, "wonders" cause amazement, and "powers" are mighty works.

decisions.choice: distributions of the Holy Spirit, given as God wills
alternatives: distributions made by the Holy Spirit according to the Spirit's will
decisions.reason: "Distributions of the Holy Spirit" may mean gifts that God gives out by the Spirit, or the Spirit himself given in portions to believers. "His will" refers to God, who is the subject of this part of the sentence. Elsewhere it is the Spirit who distributes gifts as he wills (1 Corinthians 12:11).

decisions.choice: the question ends at "as great as this?"; the rest becomes statements
decisions.reason: The Greek is one long question. Balanced ends the question once its point is made, and puts the clauses about how the message came in a new sentence.

decisions.choice: God gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} law through angels; the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says outright that the word spoken through angels is God's law (m1) and that "the Lord" is Jesus (m6).

decisions.choice: was punished as they deserved
decisions.reason: Readable says "punished as they deserved" for "received a just recompense".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían escuchado
decisions.reason: For a male person as direct object Spanish in Latin America uses "lo" and much of Spain uses "le". The text uses "lo", the form understood everywhere; the plural_you setting does not cover this difference.

decisions.choice: malipo yaliyostahili (L); adhabu iliyostahili (B); aliadhibiwa kama alivyostahili (R)
decisions.reason: "Haki" is kept for righteousness, a key term (1:9). Here the Greek word means a penalty that fits the offence, which "-stahili" (deserved) says without borrowing that word.

decisions.choice: miujiza (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "miracles" for the "powers", as the English Readable does; "ishara" stays for "signs" at every level, so the two Greek words remain distinct.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ ἀγγέλοις ὑπέταξεν τὴν οἰκουμένην τὴν μέλλουσαν, περὶ ἧς λαλοῦμεν·

records.literal_gloss: Not for to angels did he subject the inhabited world the coming, about which we are speaking;

en.L: For not to angels did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} subject the coming inhabited world, about which we are speaking;
en.B: For God did not place the world to come, the world we are talking about, under the rule of angels.
en.R: God did not put angels in charge of the new world that is coming. That is the world we are talking about.

es.L: Porque no a ángeles sometió el mundo habitado venidero, del cual estamos hablando;
es.B: Porque Dios no puso bajo el gobierno de los ángeles el mundo venidero, el mundo del que estamos hablando.
es.R: Dios no puso a los ángeles al mando del mundo nuevo que viene. Ese es el mundo del que estamos hablando.

sw.L: Kwa maana si malaika aliowatiishia ulimwengu ujao unaokaliwa, ambao tunauzungumzia;
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu hakuuweka ulimwengu ujao, ule tunaouzungumzia, chini ya utawala wa malaika.
sw.R: Mungu hakuwapa malaika mamlaka juu ya ulimwengu mpya unaokuja. Huo ndio ulimwengu tunaouzungumzia.

decisions.choice: the coming inhabited world: the new order God is bringing, already begun with the Son's enthronement
decisions.reason: οἰκουμένη is the word used in 1:6 for the world into which God brings the firstborn. "The coming world" is the new age of salvation, which believers already taste (6:5) and will fully enter (13:14, "the city to come").

decisions.choice: not to angels: the present world was thought to be under angelic powers
decisions.reason: According to Deuteronomy 32:8 in the Greek, God divided the nations "according to the number of the angels of God", and Daniel 10:13, 20 speaks of angelic princes over nations. The author may be contrasting that with the world to come, which God has subjected not to angels but to the human being of Psalm 8, fulfilled in Jesus.

decisions.choice: subject: the verb that the quotation of Psalm 8 takes up
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσω, "put under, subject", is the verb of Psalm 8:6, quoted in verse 8 ("you subjected all things under his feet"). The author chooses it to lead into the psalm.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "he subjected"; the subject is God, as in chapter 1, so Balanced and Readable name him.

decisions.choice: the world (R: the new world that is coming)
decisions.reason: Literal says "inhabited world" as at 1:6; Balanced and Readable say "world".

decisions.choice: aliowatiishia (kutiisha)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "kutiisha" (to put under) because the quotation of Psalm 8 that follows uses the same verb (verse 8, "ulivitiisha"), and meaning decision m3 says the author chose this word to lead into it.

source.text: διεμαρτύρατο δέ πού τις λέγων· Τί ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι μιμνῄσκῃ αὐτοῦ, ἢ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὅτι ἐπισκέπτῃ αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Testified but somewhere someone saying, What is man that you remember him, or son of man that you look after him?

en.L: But someone has testified somewhere, saying, "What is {{gender:a human being|man}} that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} remember him, or [the] son of man that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look after him?
en.B: But there is a place where someone has testified, "What is {{gender:a human being|man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} remember him, or {{gender:a mortal|the son of man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} watch over him?
en.R: Somewhere in Scripture someone says this to God: "What is {{gender:a human being|man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} should think of him? What is {{gender:a mere mortal|the son of man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} should take care of him?

es.L: Pero alguien ha testificado en algún lugar, diciendo: «¿Qué es el {{gender:ser humano|hombre}} para que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acuerdes de él, o [el] hijo de hombre para que lo cuides?
es.B: Pero hay un lugar donde alguien ha dado testimonio: «¿Qué es el {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acuerdes de él, o {{gender:un mortal|el hijo del hombre}}, para que lo cuides?
es.R: En algún lugar de las Escrituras alguien dice esto a Dios: «¿Qué es el {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}, para que pienses en él? ¿Qué es {{gender:un simple mortal|el hijo del hombre}}, para que cuides de él?

sw.L: Lakini mtu fulani mahali fulani ameshuhudia, akisema, "Mwanadamu ni nini, kwamba unamkumbuka, au mwana wa mtu, kwamba unamtunza?
sw.B: Lakini kuna mahali ambapo mtu fulani ameshuhudia, "Binadamu ni nini, kwamba unamkumbuka, au mwanadamu, kwamba unamjali?
sw.R: Mahali fulani katika Maandiko mtu fulani anamwambia Mungu hivi: "Mwanadamu ni nini mpaka umfikirie? Binadamu dhaifu ni nini mpaka umtunze?

decisions.choice: someone has testified somewhere: a way of citing Scripture by its message, not its human author
decisions.reason: The author knows the source well (Psalm 8, a psalm of David), but in Hebrews what matters is that God speaks in Scripture (1:5-13; 3:7), so the human speaker can be left vague. He cites Genesis 2:2 the same way in 4:4.

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:4-6
decisions.reason: Verses 6-8 quote Psalm 8:4-6 (8:5-7 in the Hebrew and Greek numbering) in the wording of the Greek translation. The psalm marvels that God has given weak humankind honor and rule over his works (Genesis 1:26-28).

decisions.choice: the psalm speaks of humankind; the author reads it of Jesus in verse 9
alternatives: the author reads the whole psalm as about Jesus from the start
decisions.reason: In the psalm "man" and "son of man" are parallel ways of saying "human being": "son of man" is not here the title Jesus uses of himself in the Gospels. The psalm speaks of humankind's God-given place. In verse 8 the author observes that this rule is not yet seen, and in verse 9 he sees it fulfilled in Jesus, the one human being already crowned with glory and honor, who brings many others to glory (verse 10). Some read the psalm as about Jesus from the start of the quotation.

decisions.choice: remember, look after: God keeps the human being in mind and cares for him
decisions.reason: μιμνῄσκομαι is "remember, be mindful of". ἐπισκέπτομαι is "visit, look upon", used of God coming to help and care for his people (Luke 1:68).

decisions.choice: {{gender:a human being|man}}; {{gender:a mortal|the son of man}}
alternatives: What are human beings, that you remember them
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of human beings in general, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default, with the traditional "man" and "the son of man" as the alternative. Literal keeps "son of man", lowercase, since it is the psalm's name for a human being and not a title. The pronoun "him" is kept singular, because the author goes on to apply the psalm to one man, Jesus (verse 9); it takes no deity_pronoun span, since in the psalm it is the human being.

decisions.choice: Somewhere in Scripture someone says this to God
decisions.reason: Readable says that the words are from Scripture and are spoken to God, since "you" in the psalm is God.

decisions.choice: el {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}; {{gender:un mortal|el hijo del hombre}} (B), {{gender:un simple mortal|el hijo del hombre}} (R)
decisions.reason: Unlike "hermanos", Spanish "el hombre" is often heard as a male, so here the inclusive "ser humano" is the default, as the English has it. "Él" and "lo" for the human being of the psalm stay as they are: they refer back to "ser humano", a masculine noun, and take no deity_pronoun span (see the English r-en-1 on verse 7).

decisions.choice: mwanadamu, binadamu, mwana wa mtu: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Swahili "mwanadamu", "binadamu" and "mtu" already mean a human being, man or woman, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change; the only male word, "mwanamume", would change the meaning. Literal says "mwana wa mtu", not the title "Mwana wa Adamu", because the psalm speaks of humankind (meaning decision m3) and the title would decide in advance that it speaks of Jesus.

source.text: ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους, δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφάνωσας αὐτόν, πάντα ὑπέταξας ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· ἐν τῷ γὰρ ὑποτάξαι τὰ πάντα οὐδὲν ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ ἀνυπότακτον.

records.literal_gloss: You made lower him a little some than angels, with glory and honor you crowned him, \v 8 all things you subjected under the feet of him. In the for to subject the all things nothing he left to him unsubjected.

en.L: You made him a little lower than [the] angels; with glory and honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crowned him; \v 8 all things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} subjected under his feet." For in subjecting all things [to him], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left nothing unsubjected to him.
en.B: You made him a little lower than the angels; with glory and honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crowned him, \v 8 and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put all things in subjection under his feet." When God subjected all things to him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left nothing that is not subject to him.
en.R: You made him a little lower than the angels. You gave him glory and honor like a crown. \v 8 You put everything under his feet." When God put everything under him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left nothing out.

es.L: Lo hiciste un poco inferior a [los] ángeles; de gloria y de honra lo coronaste; \v 8 todo lo sometiste bajo sus pies». Porque al someter[le] todas las cosas, nada dejó que no le estuviera sometido.
es.B: Lo hiciste un poco inferior a los ángeles; lo coronaste de gloria y de honra, \v 8 y pusiste todas las cosas bajo sus pies». Cuando Dios le sometió todas las cosas, no dejó nada que no le estuviera sometido.
es.R: Lo hiciste un poco inferior a los ángeles. Le diste gloria y honra como una corona. \v 8 Pusiste todo bajo sus pies». Cuando Dios le sometió todo, no dejó nada fuera.

sw.L: Ulimfanya kuwa chini kidogo kuliko malaika; kwa utukufu na heshima ulimvika taji; \v 8 vitu vyote ulivitiisha chini ya miguu yake." Kwa maana katika kutiisha vitu vyote [kwake], hakumwachia kitu chochote kisichotiishwa.
sw.B: Ulimfanya kuwa chini kidogo kuliko malaika; kwa utukufu na heshima ulimvika taji, \v 8 na ukaweka vitu vyote chini ya miguu yake." Mungu alipomtiishia vitu vyote, hakuacha kitu chochote ambacho hakijawekwa chini yake.
sw.R: Ulimfanya chini kidogo kuliko malaika. Ulimpa utukufu na heshima kama taji. \v 8 Uliweka kila kitu chini ya miguu yake." Mungu alipoweka kila kitu chini yake, hakuacha kitu chochote nje.

decisions.choice: Psalm 8:5-6 (Greek), continued: "angels"
decisions.reason: The quotation of Psalm 8 continues. Where the Greek has "lower than angels", the Hebrew has "lower than God" (or "than heavenly beings"), since the Hebrew word can mean God, gods, or the beings of God's court. The author follows the Greek, which suits his comparison of the Son with the angels.

decisions.choice: the quotation omits "and you set him over the works of your hands" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: you crowned him with glory and honor, and set him over the works of your hands
decisions.reason: After "you crowned him", many manuscripts (among them Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi and Bezae) add "and you set him over the works of your hands", the next line of the Greek psalm. The SBL text leaves it out, with the oldest papyrus (P46), Vaticanus and the later majority of manuscripts. The longer text may have been filled in from the psalm by copyists. This description is from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a little lower: lower by a small degree, as the psalm means it
decisions.reason: βραχύ τι can mean "a little" in degree or "for a little while" in time. In the psalm it is degree: humankind is only a little below the beings of heaven. In verse 9 the author seems to use the same words of time, for Jesus' brief humbling (see the decision there).

decisions.choice: in subjecting all things, he left nothing unsubjected: the author presses the word "all"
decisions.reason: The author comments on the psalm: "all things" means everything, with nothing left out. That makes the next statement sharper: all things are not yet seen subjected to the human being (verse 8b). The subject is God, as in the psalm.

decisions.choice: him (no deity_pronoun span)
decisions.reason: In the psalm "him" is the human being, so it takes no deity_pronoun span, though verse 9 applies the psalm to Jesus. "You" is God, addressed in the psalm, and takes the span.

decisions.choice: gave him glory and honor like a crown
alternatives: crowned him with glory and honor
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of crowning; it keeps "glory" as every level does.

source.text: νῦν δὲ οὔπω ὁρῶμεν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ὑποτεταγμένα·

records.literal_gloss: Now but not yet do we see to him the all things having been subjected;

en.L: But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him;
en.B: But as it is, we do not yet see all things put under him.
en.R: But we do not yet see everything put under human beings.

es.L: Pero ahora todavía no vemos que todas las cosas le estén sometidas;
es.B: Pero tal como están las cosas, todavía no vemos que todo esté puesto bajo él.
es.R: Pero todavía no vemos que todo esté bajo el poder de los seres humanos.

sw.L: Lakini sasa bado hatuoni vitu vyote vimetiishwa kwake;
sw.B: Lakini kama ilivyo sasa, bado hatuoni vitu vyote vikiwa chini yake.
sw.R: Lakini bado hatuoni kila kitu kikiwa chini ya wanadamu.

decisions.choice: him: the human being of the psalm, that is, humankind
alternatives: Jesus, whose enemies are not yet all subjected
decisions.reason: The author has just applied "all things" strictly. Now he observes that humankind does not yet rule over everything as the psalm says. Then he turns to the one in whom the psalm is already fulfilled: "but we see Jesus" (verse 9). Some take "him" here already as Jesus, whose rule is not yet complete (compare 10:13).

decisions.choice: but now, not yet: the present contrasted with what God has promised
decisions.reason: "Now ... not yet" sets the present state of the world against the psalm's promise. The fulfillment has begun in Jesus but is not complete.

decisions.choice: human beings
decisions.reason: Readable says "human beings" for "him", following meaning decision m1, so that a young reader can follow the argument. Literal and Balanced keep "him".

source.text: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον, ὅπως χωρὶς θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] but for a little some than angels having been made lower we see, Jesus, because of the suffering of the death with glory and honor having been crowned, so that apart from God for everyone he might taste death.

en.L: But we see the one made lower than [the] angels for a little [while], Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that apart from God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might taste death for everyone.
en.B: But Jesus we do see. For a little while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was placed lower than the angels, and because of the death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} suffered {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been crowned with glory and honor, so that apart from God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should taste death on behalf of everyone.
en.R: But we do see Jesus. For a short time God made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} lower than the angels. Jesus suffered death, and because of that God has crowned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with glory and honor. So, apart from God, Jesus went through death for everyone.

es.L: Pero vemos al que por un poco [de tiempo] fue hecho inferior a [los] ángeles, a Jesús, coronado de gloria y de honra a causa del padecimiento de la muerte, para que aparte de Dios gustara la muerte por todos.
es.B: Pero a Jesús sí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vemos. Por un poco de tiempo fue puesto en un lugar inferior a los ángeles, y a causa de la muerte que sufrió ha sido coronado de gloria y de honra, para que, aparte de Dios, gustara la muerte a favor de todos.
es.R: Pero sí vemos a Jesús. Por un tiempo corto Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso por debajo de los ángeles. Jesús sufrió la muerte, y por eso Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha coronado de gloria y de honra. Así, aparte de Dios, Jesús pasó por la muerte a favor de todos.

sw.L: Lakini yule aliyefanywa kwa muda kidogo kuwa chini kuliko malaika tunamwona, Yesu, akiwa amevikwa taji kwa utukufu na heshima kwa sababu ya mateso ya kifo, ili mbali na Mungu aonje kifo kwa ajili ya kila mtu.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu tunamwona. Kwa muda mfupi aliwekwa chini kuliko malaika, na kwa sababu ya kifo alichokiteseka amevikwa taji kwa utukufu na heshima, ili mbali na Mungu aonje kifo kwa ajili ya kila mtu.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu tunamwona. Kwa muda mfupi Mungu alimweka chini kuliko malaika. Yesu aliteseka hadi kufa, na kwa sababu hiyo Mungu amempa utukufu na heshima kama taji. Kwa hiyo, mbali na Mungu, Yesu alipitia kifo kwa ajili ya kila mtu.

decisions.choice: apart from God (SBLGNT), not "by the grace of God"
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, including the oldest (P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus), read "by the grace of God". The SBL text instead reads "apart from God", found in very few manuscripts but known to several writers of the early centuries, among them Origen, who knew both readings. It is the harder reading: a copyist could easily have changed the startling "apart from God" into the familiar "by the grace of God" (the two Greek words look alike), but hardly the reverse. The SBL text governs here; the footnote gives the other reading. This description is from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: apart from God: Jesus went through death fully, without God sparing him
alternatives: for everyone except God (for all things but God)
decisions.reason: If "apart from God" is the right text, it most likely means that Jesus tasted death for everyone fully, as one left without God's help (compare 5:7 and Psalm 22:1, the psalm that verse 12 quotes). Others take it with "everyone": he died for everything except God himself, since God is not among the "all things" subjected (verse 8; compare 1 Corinthians 15:27). Either way it does not say that the Son was cut off from God in his being.

decisions.choice: for a little while
decisions.reason: The words of the psalm (verse 7) are taken up again. Here, set between suffering and crowning, they most naturally speak of time: Jesus was lower than the angels for a short while, in his earthly life and death, and is now crowned. The phrase can also mean "a little" in degree, as in the psalm.

decisions.choice: Jesus named for the first time; the purpose of the whole humbling
decisions.reason: The author names Jesus for the first time in the letter, holding the name back to the end of the phrase for emphasis. The "so that" clause gives the purpose of the whole sequence: he was made lower and suffered death, and so was crowned, in order that his death might be for everyone.

decisions.choice: taste death: experience death in full
decisions.reason: "Taste death" is a Jewish idiom for actually dying (Mark 9:1; John 8:52). It does not mean a mere sip of death.

decisions.choice: for everyone: on behalf of every person
decisions.reason: παντὸς could be masculine ("everyone") or neuter ("everything"). The following verses speak of people: many sons, brothers and sisters, children (verses 10-14). ὑπέρ means "on behalf of, for the sake of".

decisions.choice: God made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who made Jesus lower, as the psalm says ("you made him", verse 7), and says "went through death" for "taste death".

decisions.choice: mbali na Mungu (apart from God)
decisions.reason: "Bila Mungu" can sound like "godless" or "without God's help". "Mbali na Mungu" says that Jesus went through death fully, apart from God, which is how meaning decision m2 reads the SBL text.

source.text: Ἔπρεπεν γὰρ αὐτῷ, δι’ ὃν τὰ πάντα καὶ δι’ οὗ τὰ πάντα, πολλοὺς υἱοὺς εἰς δόξαν ἀγαγόντα τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν διὰ παθημάτων τελειῶσαι.

records.literal_gloss: It was fitting for to him, for whom the all things and through whom the all things, many sons to glory having brought, the pioneer of the salvation of them through sufferings to make perfect.

en.L: For it was fitting for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for whom [are] all things and through whom [are] all things, in bringing many {{gender:children|sons}} to glory, to make the pioneer of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
en.B: For God, for whose sake everything exists and through whom everything exists, was bringing many {{gender:children|sons}} to glory, and so it was right for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bring to perfection through sufferings the pioneer who leads them to salvation.
en.R: God made everything, and everything exists for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is bringing many {{gender:children|sons}} to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory. So it was right for God to make Jesus complete by letting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} suffer. Jesus is the pioneer who leads them to salvation.

es.L: Porque convenía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, por causa de quien [son] todas las cosas y por medio de quien [son] todas las cosas, al llevar a muchos hijos a la gloria, hacer perfecto por medio de sufrimientos al pionero de la salvación de ellos.
es.B: Porque Dios, por cuya causa existe todo y por medio de quien existe todo, estaba llevando a muchos hijos a la gloria, y por eso {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} convenía hacer perfecto por medio de sufrimientos al pionero que los guía a la salvación.
es.R: Dios hizo todas las cosas, y todo existe para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Está llevando a muchos hijos a compartir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria. Por eso era justo que Dios hiciera completo a Jesús permitiendo que sufriera. Jesús es el pionero que va delante y los guía a la salvación.

sw.L: Kwa maana ilimfaa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, ambaye kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} [vipo] vitu vyote na kupitia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} [vipo] vitu vyote, katika kuwaleta wana wengi kwenye utukufu, kumkamilisha kupitia mateso yule kiongozi wa wokovu wao.
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu, ambaye kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kila kitu kipo na kupitia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kila kitu kipo, alikuwa akiwaleta wana wengi kwenye utukufu. Kwa hiyo ilimfaa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kumkamilisha kupitia mateso kiongozi anayewaongoza kwenye wokovu.
sw.R: Mungu aliumba kila kitu, na kila kitu kipo kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Anawaleta wana wengi washiriki utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Kwa hiyo ilikuwa sawa Mungu amkamilishe Yesu kwa kumwacha ateseke. Yesu ndiye anayewatangulia na kuwaongoza kwenye wokovu.

decisions.choice: for him, for whom and through whom all things: God, the goal and the source of everything
decisions.reason: "Him" is God. Everything exists for him as its goal and through him as its maker (compare Romans 11:36). It was fitting for such a God, who is bringing his creation to its purpose, to act in this way.

decisions.choice: in bringing: God is the one who brings many to glory
alternatives: the pioneer, who brings many sons to glory
decisions.reason: ἀγαγόντα is accusative, while "for him" is dative. It most likely refers to God, the subject of the infinitive "to make perfect": God, in bringing many to glory, perfected their pioneer. It could instead agree with "the pioneer", who brings many to glory, but then the participle would stand oddly before the noun it describes.

decisions.choice: many sons: all believers, women and men, who share the Son's place in God's family
decisions.reason: υἱός here includes every believer, daughters as well as sons (2 Corinthians 6:18). The word links them with "the Son" of chapter 1: those he saves become God's children with him (2:11-13; 12:5-8).

decisions.choice: pioneer: the leader who goes first and opens the way for others to follow
decisions.reason: ἀρχηγός can mean leader, founder, or originator: one who begins something and leads others into it. Jesus goes ahead through suffering into glory and brings his people after him. The word returns in 12:2, of Jesus as pioneer and perfecter of faith.

decisions.choice: make perfect: bring to the goal, make fully fit for his office as Savior and high priest
decisions.reason: τελειόω means "complete, bring to the goal, make fully what one is meant to be". Jesus was never imperfect in a moral sense; he was without sin (4:15; 7:26). Through suffering he was made fully fit for his calling: having learned obedience by what he suffered, he became the source of salvation and a high priest for ever (5:8-10; 7:28). In the Greek Old Testament the same verb is used for the consecration of priests to their office (Exodus 29:9, 29:33; Leviticus 16:32). The word family runs through Hebrews: the law made nothing perfect (7:19), but Christ has perfected those who are made holy (10:14). Later chapters refer back to this decision.

decisions.choice: to glory: to share in the glory with which Jesus has been crowned
decisions.reason: The glory is the honor God gives, which Jesus already has (verse 9) and into which he leads the many. It is the fulfillment of Psalm 8, where God crowns humankind with glory and honor.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The many brought to glory are women and men, so the gender setting gives "children" by default, with "sons" as the traditional alternative. The alternative keeps the link with "the Son"; meaning decision m3 explains it.

decisions.choice: make complete
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "perfect" so that the word family can be followed through the letter. Readable says "make complete", because "perfect" suggests to most readers that Jesus once had faults; meaning decision m5 explains the sense.

decisions.choice: share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus as the pioneer and says that the many share in God's glory (m6).

decisions.choice: pioneer
decisions.reason: "Pioneer" says both that Jesus goes first and that he opens the way for others (m4). Balanced adds "who leads them" to make the second point clear.

decisions.choice: hijos, no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English offers "children" with "sons" as the traditional form. Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters and keeps the heir's standing the meaning decision (m3) describes, so, as in Ephesians 1:5, no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: pionero (for the whole letter, also 12:2)
decisions.reason: "Autor" now suggests a writer or one who causes something, and "capitán" a military rank. "Pionero" is the one who goes ahead and opens the way for others to follow (m4). Readable adds "que va delante" so the picture is plain.

decisions.choice: wana, no gender setting (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Wana" (children of a parent, sons and daughters) already includes women, so the Swahili has no gender span where the English has {{gender:children|sons}}. It keeps the link with "Mwana", the Son, which meaning decision m3 draws on. The same holds in 12:5-8.

decisions.choice: kiongozi (L, B); anayewatangulia na kuwaongoza (R) (for the whole letter, also 12:2)
decisions.reason: "Kiongozi" is a leader; Balanced adds "anayewaongoza" (who leads them) and Readable uses verbs, "goes ahead of them and leads them", to bring out the sense of one who goes first and opens the way (meaning decision m4). "Mwanzilishi" (founder) would lose the picture of going ahead.

source.text: ὅ τε γὰρ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντες· δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοὺς καλεῖν, λέγων· Ἀπαγγελῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου, ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας ὑμνήσω σε·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] both for sanctifying and those being sanctified of one all; for which reason not he is ashamed brothers them to call, \v 12 saying, I will announce the name of you to the brothers of me, in [the] midst of [the] assembly I will sing hymns to you;

en.L: For both the one sanctifying and those being sanctified [are] all from one; for which reason {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not ashamed to call them {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, \v 12 saying, "I will announce {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; in [the] midst of [the] assembly I will sing hymns to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: For the one who makes holy and those who are being made holy all come from one source. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not ashamed to call them {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. \v 12 He says, "I will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name known to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}; in the middle of the assembly I will sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise."
en.R: Jesus makes people holy. He and the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes holy all come from the same Father. That is why Jesus is not ashamed to call them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. \v 12 He says to God, "I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. I will sing praises to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the middle of the gathered people."

es.L: Porque tanto el que santifica como los que son santificados [son] todos de uno; por esa causa no se avergüenza de llamarlos hermanos, \v 12 diciendo: «Anunciaré {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos; en medio de [la] asamblea {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré himnos».
es.B: Porque el que santifica y los que son santificados proceden todos de un mismo origen. Por eso no se avergüenza de llamarlos hermanos. \v 12 Dice: «Daré a conocer {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos; en medio de la asamblea cantaré {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} alabanzas».
es.R: Jesús hace santos a otros. Él y los que hace santos vienen todos del mismo Padre. Por eso Jesús no se avergüenza de llamarlos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos. \v 12 Dice a Dios: «Les diré a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos quién eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}. Te cantaré alabanzas en medio del pueblo reunido».

sw.L: Kwa maana yule anayetakasa na wale wanaotakaswa wote ni wa mmoja; ndiyo sababu haoni aibu kuwaita ndugu, \v 12 akisema, "Nitawatangazia ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; katikati ya kusanyiko nitakusifu kwa nyimbo."
sw.B: Kwa maana yule anayetakasa na wale wanaotakaswa wote wanatoka katika chanzo kimoja. Ndiyo sababu haoni aibu kuwaita ndugu. \v 12 Anasema, "Nitawajulisha ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}; katikati ya kusanyiko nitaimba sifa {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}."
sw.R: Yesu huwafanya watu kuwa watakatifu. Yeye na wale anaowafanya watakatifu wote wanatoka kwa Baba yule yule. Ndiyo sababu Yesu haoni aibu kuwaita ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. \v 12 Anamwambia Mungu, "Nitawaeleza ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} jinsi {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulivyo. Nitakuimbia sifa katikati ya watu waliokusanyika."

decisions.choice: sanctify: make holy, set apart for God and cleansed
decisions.reason: ἁγιάζω means to make holy: to set apart for God and make fit to come near him. Jesus does it by his own blood (10:10, 10:14; 13:12). The present tense "those being sanctified" describes believers as the people in whom this work is going on.

decisions.choice: all from one: from one Father, God
decisions.reason: "From one" is left open in the Greek. Most likely it is God, the Father of the Son and of the many sons and daughters he brings to glory (verse 10). It could also mean one ancestor (Adam, or Abraham, verse 16) or one common human nature (verse 14).

decisions.choice: brothers: the whole family of believers, women and men
decisions.reason: Jesus calls those he makes holy his brothers and sisters: they belong to one family. The word includes women, as it does when the author addresses his readers (3:1, 3:12).

decisions.choice: Psalm 22:22 (21:23 Greek)
decisions.reason: The quotation is Psalm 22:22 (21:23 in the Greek numbering). The psalm begins with the cry of a sufferer forsaken by God ("My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?", Psalm 22:1, words Jesus spoke on the cross) and turns at verse 22 to praise among God's people after God has rescued him. The author puts the words in the mouth of Jesus, who after his suffering praises God among his brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: assembly: the gathered people of God
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησία translates the Hebrew word for Israel gathered for worship. In 12:23 the same word is used of the gathering of the firstborn in heaven.

decisions.choice: your name: who God is and what he has done
decisions.reason: In Scripture a name stands for the person and his character. To announce God's name is to tell who he is and what he has done.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Those Jesus calls his brothers include women, so the gender setting applies, with the traditional "brothers" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: makes holy; being made holy
decisions.reason: Literal says "sanctify". Balanced and Readable say "make holy", which says the same in plain words, as everywhere in Hebrews.

decisions.choice: from the same Father
decisions.reason: Readable follows meaning decision m2 and names the "one" as the Father. It is uncertain, as m2 says.

decisions.choice: who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are; the gathered people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "your name" (m6) and says "the gathered people" for "the assembly".

decisions.choice: hermanos, no gender setting (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so adding "y hermanas" would add words the Greek does not have; the whole family of believers is meant (m3). This follows Romans, Philippians and Colossians. A reviewer may prefer to make the women explicit.

decisions.choice: santificar (L, B); hacer santo (R) (for the whole letter)
alternatives: hacer santo at every level, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: "Santificar" is the Spanish word for making holy and setting apart for God (m1) and stays recognisable across Hebrews (10:10, 10:14, 13:12), so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced says "makes holy". Readable says "hacer santo".

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender setting (for the whole letter)
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so the Swahili has no gender span where the English has {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, here and throughout Hebrews.

decisions.choice: kutakasa (L, B); kuwafanya watakatifu (R); kusanyiko (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Kutakasa" is the settled word for "sanctify, make holy" in Hebrews; Readable says it plainly, "make people holy", as the English Readable does. The psalm's "assembly" is "kusanyiko", the gathered people of God, not "kanisa", which would read a later word for the church back into the psalm.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν· Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ἐπ’ αὐτῷ· καὶ πάλιν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: And again, I will be trusting in him; and again, See I and the children whom to me gave the God.

en.L: And again, "I will be trusting in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}." And again, "See, I and the children whom God has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: And again, "I will go on trusting in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}." And again, "Here I am, with the children God has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: In another place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "I will keep on trusting God." He also says, "Here I am, together with the children God has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Y otra vez: «Yo estaré confiando en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}». Y otra vez: «He aquí yo y los hijos que Dios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dio».
es.B: Y otra vez: «Seguiré confiando en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}». Y otra vez: «Aquí estoy, con los hijos que Dios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado».
es.R: En otro lugar dice: «Seguiré confiando en Dios». También dice: «Aquí estoy, junto con los hijos que Dios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado».

sw.L: Na tena, "Mimi nitakuwa mwenye kumtegemea {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}." Na tena, "Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} pamoja na watoto ambao Mungu amenipa."
sw.B: Na tena, "Nitaendelea kumtumaini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}." Na tena, "Mimi hapa, pamoja na watoto ambao Mungu amenipa."
sw.R: Mahali pengine anasema, "Nitaendelea kumtegemea Mungu." Tena anasema, "Mimi hapa, pamoja na watoto ambao Mungu amenipa."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 8:17 (Greek); compare 2 Samuel 22:3 and Isaiah 12:2
decisions.reason: The words "I will trust in him" match the Greek of Isaiah 8:17, where the prophet waits for God while God hides his face from Israel. The Hebrew of Isaiah 8:17 says "I will hope in him". Similar words occur in the Greek of 2 Samuel 22:3 and Isaiah 12:2, but the next quotation, from Isaiah 8:18, shows that Isaiah 8 is meant.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 8:18
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 8:18 the prophet says that he and the children God has given him are signs to Israel; the Hebrew has the divine name, YHWH, where the Greek has "God". The author hears in it the voice of Jesus, standing with the people God has given him.

decisions.choice: I will be trusting: Jesus, as a human being, lived in steady trust in God
decisions.reason: The construction ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ("I will be one who trusts") describes a lasting state. The point is that Jesus shares the life of those he saves: like them he depended on God and trusted him (5:7; 12:2).

decisions.choice: the children: believers, the family God has given to Jesus
decisions.reason: παιδίον are the "many sons" of verse 10 and the brothers and sisters of verses 11-12. They are God's gift to Jesus (compare John 6:37; 17:6).

decisions.choice: Here I am
decisions.reason: The word traditionally rendered "behold" calls for attention; Balanced and Readable say "Here I am", and Literal "See".

decisions.choice: In another place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says; trusting God
decisions.reason: Readable says that these are further words of Jesus from Scripture, and names God as the one he trusts.

source.text: Ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ παιδία κεκοινώνηκεν αἵματος καὶ σαρκός, καὶ αὐτὸς παραπλησίως μετέσχεν τῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα διὰ τοῦ θανάτου καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου, τοῦτ’ ἔστι τὸν διάβολον, καὶ ἀπαλλάξῃ τούτους, ὅσοι φόβῳ θανάτου διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας.

records.literal_gloss: Since therefore the children have shared in blood and flesh, also he likewise partook of the same, so that through the death he might render powerless the [one] the power having of the death, that is, the devil, \v 15 and might set free these, as many as by fear of death through all the to live subject were to slavery.

en.L: Since then the children have had a share of blood and flesh, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} also in like manner had a part in the same [things], so that through death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might render powerless the one having the power of death, that is, the devil, \v 15 and set free those who, by fear of death, through all [their] living were subject to slavery.
en.B: Since the children, then, share a common life of flesh and blood, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} took on that same life in the same way, so that by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might strip of power the one who holds the power of death, the devil, \v 15 and release those whom the fear of death kept enslaved their whole life long.
en.R: These children are human beings, with flesh and blood. So Jesus also became a human being like them. He died, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took away all the power of the devil, who had the power of death. \v 15 All their lives people were slaves to their fear of death. Jesus died to set them free.

es.L: Así que, puesto que los hijos han participado de sangre y carne, también {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} de igual manera tomó parte de lo mismo, para que por medio de la muerte dejara sin poder al que tenía el poder de la muerte, es decir, al diablo, \v 15 y librara a todos estos que por temor a la muerte estaban sujetos a esclavitud durante toda [su] vida.
es.B: Ya que los hijos, entonces, comparten una misma vida de carne y sangre, {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} tomó esa misma vida de igual manera, para que por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte despojara de su poder al que tiene el poder de la muerte, el diablo, \v 15 y librara a los que el miedo a la muerte tenía esclavizados durante toda su vida.
es.R: Estos hijos son seres humanos, con carne y sangre. Por eso Jesús también se hizo ser humano como ellos. Murió, y por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte le quitó todo su poder al diablo, que tenía el poder de la muerte. \v 15 Durante toda su vida la gente vivía esclava de su miedo a la muerte. Jesús murió para liberarla.

sw.L: Basi kwa kuwa watoto wamekuwa na sehemu katika damu na mwili, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} pia kwa namna iliyo sawa alipata sehemu katika [mambo] hayo hayo, ili kupitia kifo amvunjie nguvu yule aliye na mamlaka ya kifo, yaani, Ibilisi, \v 15 na kuwaweka huru wale wote ambao, kwa kuogopa kifo, katika kuishi kwao kote walikuwa wamefungwa katika utumwa.
sw.B: Basi, kwa kuwa watoto wanashiriki maisha ya pamoja ya mwili na damu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliyapokea maisha hayo hayo kwa namna ile ile, ili kwa kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} amnyang'anye nguvu yule anayeshika mamlaka ya kifo, yaani Ibilisi, \v 15 na kuwaweka huru wale ambao hofu ya kifo iliwaweka utumwani maisha yao yote.
sw.R: Watoto hao ni wanadamu wenye mwili na damu. Kwa hiyo Yesu naye akawa mwanadamu kama wao. Alikufa, na kwa kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} aliondoa nguvu zote za Ibilisi, aliyekuwa na nguvu ya kifo. \v 15 Maisha yao yote watu walikuwa watumwa wa hofu yao ya kifo. Yesu alikufa ili awaweke huru.

decisions.choice: blood and flesh: human nature, weak and mortal
decisions.reason: "Blood and flesh" (in this order also in Ephesians 6:12) means human beings in their frailty and mortality (compare Matthew 16:17).

decisions.choice: the children share it; he took part in it: the Son became human by his own choice
decisions.reason: The children "have shared" (perfect tense): human nature is what they are. He "took part" (aorist): at a point in time he took the same nature on himself. παραπλησίως ("in the same way, likewise") stresses that his humanity was real and not a mere appearance.

decisions.choice: render powerless: break the devil's hold, bring his power to nothing
decisions.reason: καταργέω means "make ineffective, abolish, render powerless". The devil is not said to cease to exist, but his power over death, and so over those who fear it, is broken.

decisions.choice: the one who holds the power of death: the devil
decisions.reason: Death came into the world through sin, after the serpent's deceit (Genesis 3; Romans 5:12), and the Wisdom of Solomon says that death entered the world through the devil's envy (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). Jesus called the devil a murderer from the beginning (John 8:44). By dying, Jesus took away the hold the devil had through death.

decisions.choice: slavery through fear of death: a whole life held captive by dread of dying
decisions.reason: δουλεία is slavery. The fear of death enslaves because it rules a person's choices for the whole of life. Jesus, who went through death, sets free those who were held by that fear.

decisions.choice: flesh and blood
decisions.reason: The Greek says "blood and flesh"; Literal keeps that order. Balanced and Readable use the usual order "flesh and blood", which means the same.

decisions.choice: So Jesus also became a human being like them; Jesus died to set them free
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and says plainly that "took part in the same things" means he became a human being. It breaks the long sentence and repeats the point of his death in verse 15.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ δήπου ἀγγέλων ἐπιλαμβάνεται, ἀλλὰ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ ἐπιλαμβάνεται.

records.literal_gloss: Not for surely angels he takes hold of, but [the] seed of Abraham he takes hold of.

en.L: For surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not take hold of angels, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes hold of [the] seed of Abraham.
en.B: For it is clear that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not take hold of angels to help them; it is Abraham's descendants that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes hold of.
en.R: It is clear that Jesus does not reach out to help angels. He reaches out to help Abraham's descendants.

es.L: Porque ciertamente no echa mano de ángeles, sino que echa mano de [la] simiente de Abraham.
es.B: Porque es evidente que no echa mano de los ángeles para ayudarlos; es de los descendientes de Abraham de quienes echa mano.
es.R: Es claro que Jesús no extiende la mano para ayudar a los ángeles. Extiende la mano para ayudar a los descendientes de Abraham.

sw.L: Kwa maana hakika si malaika anaowashika, bali anaushika uzao wa Ibrahimu.
sw.B: Kwa maana ni wazi kwamba hawashiki malaika ili kuwasaidia; ni wazao wa Ibrahimu ndio anaowashika.
sw.R: Ni wazi kwamba Yesu hawanyooshei malaika mkono ili kuwasaidia. Anawanyooshea mkono wazao wa Ibrahimu ili kuwasaidia.

decisions.choice: take hold of: grasp in order to help and rescue
decisions.reason: ἐπιλαμβάνομαι means "take hold of, grasp", often to help someone. Hebrews uses it in 8:9 of God taking Israel by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. An older reading took it as "take on (the nature of)", as if the verse said that Christ took on human nature rather than angelic nature; but the verb does not have that sense.

decisions.choice: the seed of Abraham: Abraham's descendants, God's people
decisions.reason: "The seed of Abraham" means Abraham's descendants, the people of God's promise (Isaiah 41:8-10), and so the people of faith whom Jesus helps (compare Galatians 3:29). It may also show that the author's readers knew themselves as heirs of Israel.

decisions.choice: surely: as everyone knows
decisions.reason: δήπου means "of course, surely": the author appeals to something the readers can see for themselves.

decisions.choice: take hold of ... to help them (R: reaches out to help)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "to help them" to show why he takes hold of them (m1); Readable says "reaches out to help".

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus as the subject.

source.text: ὅθεν ὤφειλεν κατὰ πάντα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὁμοιωθῆναι, ἵνα ἐλεήμων γένηται καὶ πιστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, εἰς τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: From where he was obligated in all things to the brothers to be made like, so that merciful he might become and faithful high priest [in] the things toward the God, for the to make atonement for the sins of the people;

en.L: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was obligated to be made like [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in all things, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might become a merciful and faithful high priest [in] the things relating to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
en.B: That is why it was necessary for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to become like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every way, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might be a merciful and faithful high priest in all that has to do with God, making atonement for the sins of the people.
en.R: So Jesus had to become like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every way. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could become a high priest who is merciful and faithful as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} serves God. As high priest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would take away the sins of the people.

es.L: Por lo cual estaba obligado a ser hecho semejante en todo a [{{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}] hermanos, para llegar a ser un sumo sacerdote misericordioso y fiel [en] las cosas que se refieren a Dios, para hacer expiación por los pecados del pueblo.
es.B: Por eso era necesario que se hiciera semejante a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos en todo, para ser un sumo sacerdote misericordioso y fiel en todo lo que tiene que ver con Dios, y hacer expiación por los pecados del pueblo.
es.R: Por eso Jesús tuvo que hacerse igual a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos en todo. Así podía llegar a ser un sumo sacerdote misericordioso y fiel en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} servicio a Dios. Como sumo sacerdote, quitaría los pecados del pueblo.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo alipaswa katika mambo yote kufanywa sawa na ndugu [{{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}], ili awe kuhani mkuu mwenye huruma na mwaminifu [katika] mambo yaliyo kwa Mungu, kwa ajili ya kufanya upatanisho wa dhambi za watu.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu ilikuwa lazima afanane na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa kila namna, ili awe kuhani mkuu mwenye huruma na mwaminifu katika yote yanayomhusu Mungu, akifanya upatanisho kwa ajili ya dhambi za watu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yesu alilazimika kuwa kama ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa kila namna. Ndipo angeweza kuwa kuhani mkuu mwenye huruma na mwaminifu anapomtumikia Mungu. Kama kuhani mkuu angeziondoa dhambi za watu.

decisions.choice: was obligated to be made like them in all things: it was necessary for his task
decisions.reason: ὀφείλω is "owe, be obligated". Given what he came to do, Jesus had to share his brothers' and sisters' life in every respect: their flesh and blood, testing and death. Hebrews 4:15 adds the one exception, that he did not sin.

decisions.choice: high priest: the chief priest of Israel, who once a year made atonement for the people
decisions.reason: This is the first time Hebrews calls Jesus high priest, the theme of 4:14 to 10:18. In Israel the high priest alone entered the Most Holy Place, once a year on the Day of Atonement, with blood for his own sins and the people's (Leviticus 16).

decisions.choice: merciful and faithful: compassionate toward people, faithful toward God
decisions.reason: A good high priest must feel with the weak (5:2) and be faithful to the one who appointed him (3:2, where Jesus is compared with faithful Moses). πιστός means "faithful, trustworthy".

decisions.choice: the things relating to God: priestly service toward God
decisions.reason: "The things toward God" is a set phrase for the priest's service on behalf of the people before God (5:1).

decisions.choice: make atonement for the sins: deal with sins so that they no longer stand between the people and God
decisions.reason: ἱλάσκομαι is the word family of the Day of Atonement and the mercy seat (9:5). With "the sins" as its object it means to remove or cover sins, the barrier between the people and God, so that God can be gracious to them. Others render it "make propitiation for", stressing that sin deserves God's anger, which is also turned away when sin is dealt with.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Those Jesus became like are women and men, so the gender setting applies, as in verses 11-12.

decisions.choice: take away
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "make atonement for". Readable says "take away", which a young reader understands, and which states the result of atonement (m5).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus as the subject.

decisions.choice: sumo sacerdote (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Sumo sacerdote" is the established Spanish name for the chief priest of Israel (m2), and it is used for the same word throughout Hebrews; "sacerdote" and "sacerdocio" are used for priest and priesthood.

decisions.choice: kuhani mkuu (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Kuhani mkuu" names the one high priest of Israel, the office Hebrews compares with Christ's. "Mkuu wa makuhani" (chief of the priests) is the word for the leading priests in the gospels, a group, and would blur that.

decisions.choice: mwenye huruma (merciful)
decisions.reason: "Huruma" is the compassion one feels for someone in trouble, which is what meaning decision m3 describes (compassionate toward people); "rehema" leans toward God's mercy in pardoning, and is kept for that (4:16).

source.text: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ πέπονθεν αὐτὸς πειρασθείς, δύναται τοῖς πειραζομένοις βοηθῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: In which for he has suffered himself having been tested, he is able those being tested to help.

en.L: For in that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has suffered, having been tested, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to help those being tested.
en.B: Having suffered {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in being tested, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to come to the aid of those who are being tested.
en.R: Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} suffered when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was put to the test. So now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is able to help others who are being put to the test.

es.L: Porque en cuanto {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} ha padecido, habiendo sido probado, puede ayudar a los que son probados.
es.B: Por haber sufrido {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} al ser puesto a prueba, puede socorrer a los que están siendo puestos a prueba.
es.R: Jesús mismo sufrió cuando fue puesto a prueba. Por eso ahora puede ayudar a otros que están siendo puestos a prueba.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa vile {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} amepitia mateso, akiwa amejaribiwa, anaweza kuwasaidia wale wanaojaribiwa.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliteseka katika kujaribiwa, anaweza kuwafikia kwa msaada wale wanaojaribiwa.
sw.R: Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliteseka alipojaribiwa. Kwa hiyo sasa anaweza kuwasaidia wengine wanaojaribiwa.

decisions.choice: tested: put to the test by suffering, which includes the pull to turn away from God's will
decisions.reason: πειράζω covers both "test" and "tempt". Here the testing is joined to suffering: Jesus felt the full pressure of pain and the fear of death to turn from the path God had given him (5:7-8; 12:2-3). In 4:15 the author says he was tested in every way as we are, yet without sin. The readers, under pressure to give up, are being tested in the same way (10:32-36; 12:3-4).

decisions.choice: in that: because
alternatives: in what he suffered when tested
decisions.reason: ἐν ᾧ most likely means "because, since". It could also mean "in the very thing in which": he can help in the very kind of suffering he went through.

decisions.choice: come to the aid of (R: help)
decisions.reason: βοηθέω is "run to help, come to the rescue"; Balanced says "come to the aid of" to keep that sense.

decisions.choice: probado, puesto a prueba
decisions.reason: "Tentar" in Spanish now means mainly to entice someone to do wrong. The meaning decision (m1) is wider: a testing by suffering that includes the pull to turn from God's will, which "probar" and "poner a prueba" cover.

decisions.choice: kujaribiwa (tested; for the whole letter, also 4:15)
decisions.reason: "Kujaribu" covers both being put to the test and being tempted, which together are what meaning decision m1 describes. "Kushawishiwa" would say only being enticed to do wrong.
